facts.statement: The genus Eopneumatosuchus was named by Crompton and Smith in 1980.
The type species of the genus is Eopneumatosuchus colberti.
Fossils of Eopneumatosuchus date to the Early Jurassic, likely the Sinemurian stage.
facts.quote: The localities probably date back to the Early Jurassic, most likely during the Sinemurian stage.

facts.statement: Eopneumatosuchus lived between 199.5 and 184.2 million years ago, from the Sinemurian to the Pliensbachian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Pliensbachian (199.5 to 184.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossil records for Eopneumatosuchus include occurrences from two localities.
Fossils of Eopneumatosuchus have been found in the Kayenta Formation of Arizona.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from two localities within the Kayenta Formation of Arizona.

facts.statement: The fossil localities are located about 20 miles southeast of the Grand Canyon and are near each other.
facts.quote: Both localities are around 20 miles southeast of the Grand Canyon and near one another.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to the complex tympanic pneumatic system of many cavities in the basicranium.
facts.quote: The basicranium had many cavities that made up a complex tympanic pneumatic system for which the genus has been named.

facts.statement: Eopneumatosuchus was initially classified as a protosuchian when it was named in 1980.
facts.quote: Eopneumatosuchus was initially considered to be a protosuchian, first proposed when the genus was named in 1980.

facts.statement: The large supratemporal fenestrae are characteristic of longirostrine crocodilians.
facts.quote: The large supratemporal fenestrae of Eopneumatosuchus are characteristic of longirostrine crocodilians.

facts.statement: Eopneumatosuchus is currently classified as a basal crocodyliform.
facts.quote: the genus is currently regarded as a basal crocodyliform.

facts.statement: Eopneumatosuchus is considered more derived than protosuchians like Protosuchus, which were found in the earlier Moenave Formation.
facts.quote: it is considered to be more derived than protosuchians such as Protosuchus, found from the Moenave Formation, whose deposition preceded that of the Kayenta Formation.

facts.statement: Eopneumatosuchus belongs to the parent group Crocodylomorpha.
Eopneumatosuchus is classified as a reptile.
Similar pneumatic cavities are found in protosuchians like Protosuchus and Hemiprotosuchus, but they are less elongated than in Eopneumatosuchus.
facts.quote: These types of cavities can also be seen in some protosuchians such as Protosuchus and Hemiprotosuchus, although they are less elongated than in Eopneumatosuchus.
